$purpose: Articles bed — peer-reviewed papers (when they're more 'article' than 'study'), online essays, long-form blog posts, working papers, definitional documents. Bridges the gap between books (long-form, edited) and studies (primary research with findings). Use this bed for the kind of thing you'd cite as 'the foundational paper on X' or 'the definitive online explainer of Y'.
$schema_notes: Each entry: id (a-<slug>), title, authors (list of names), year, venue (journal / blog / publisher), url (DOI preferred for academic), bio (FRQNCY-voice summary, 40-80 words), appears_in (topic ids), picked_in (topics that flag it as a pick), tier ('foundational' | 'definitional' | 'review' | 'commentary').

articles.title: Decentralized science (DeSci): definition, shared values, and guiding principles
articles.bio: The first attempt at a rigorous, citable definition of DeSci. Spreckelsen sets out what the term actually means, what values its practitioners share, and what guiding principles separate honest decentralised-science work from blockchain-branding. Foundational reference for anyone deciding whether a project is DeSci or just selling tokens with a research-flavoured wrapper.

articles.title: How Decentralized Science (DeSci) Improves Research
articles.bio: An accessible primer comparing centralised science to DeSci across four dimensions: funding (DAOs and quadratic funding vs grant gatekeepers), collaboration (open networks vs institutional silos), peer review (token incentives vs unpaid invisible labour), and IP (IP-NFTs vs institution-locked patents). Names the working projects worth watching — VitaDAO, ResearchHub, Molecule, Arweave, Filecoin, Ocean Protocol — and is honest about what's still hard: scalability, institutional resistance, privacy, and quality control.

articles.title: Decentralized science (DeSci) — ethereum.org
articles.venue: ethereum.org · official Ethereum Foundation use-case page
articles.bio: The canonical Ethereum Foundation explainer of DeSci. Frames the movement as public infrastructure for funding, creating, reviewing, crediting, storing, and disseminating scientific knowledge equitably. Side-by-side tables comparing DeSci vs traditional science across funding, collaboration, peer review, IP, and publication bias. Catalogues the working tooling — Molecule, VitaDAO, ResearchHub, OceanDAO, dClimate, Bio.xyz, ValleyDAO, Cerebrum, CryoDAO, IP-NFTs, soulbound tokens. Best single starting point for anyone new to the field.
